What I usually do is to tell people to start with a distribution like Debian (or a derivative like Ubuntu), and then install the major desktops (Gnome, KDE, XFCE, cinnamon, etc) and see which one they like the most. I noticed people who come from Windows aren't familiar with the fact that Linux allows you to completely swap out the user interface for another one since it's modular. I.E. if Windows 8 were more like Linux, it would have been entirely possible to get the Windows 7 desktop environment (start menu, window decorations, etc) with the Windows 8 performance improvements. It'd even be possible for Windows 10 to be using Windows 7 interface.

So you should just download some LiveCDs and experiment. You have a lot of choices with Linux (and it can be overwhelming at first), but you're not locked into something that one company tells you do to (like use Metro if you want the latest version).
